statusDetail: Atomic coverage complete across 59 catalog checks and four representative templates plus a 404 recovery path.

page.notes: Server-rendered Thai adult-video catalog. Representative paths cover listing, category, search, detail/player and 404 recovery. Login/account/checkout are absent. Playback itself was not started because player accessibility and task reachability were judgeable without consuming media.

paths.description: Homepage listing and navigation, representing the primary catalog template.
Japanese category listing, representing taxonomy/archive pages.
Search results for “test”, representing query/result state.
Representative video detail and player path, the primary consumption journey.

findings.summary: The site is fixed to a light theme.
findings.evidence: The dark-emulation screenshot is pixel-identical to the default capture; the probe reports color-scheme: normal and body background rgb(248,250,252).
findings.suggestedFix: Declare color-scheme: light dark and provide preference-driven dark surface, text, border, and media treatments.

findings.summary: High-contrast preference does not change the presentation.
findings.evidence: The prefers-contrast: more screenshot is unchanged, while Lighthouse measures text contrast as low as 2.22:1.
findings.suggestedFix: Add prefers-contrast and forced-colors treatments that preserve visible text, controls, focus, and scroll affordances.

findings.summary: Navigation swaps pages abruptly.
findings.evidence: DOM/CSS inspection found no view-transition-name or View Transition API use across listing, category, search, and detail templates.
findings.suggestedFix: Use cross-document View Transitions for same-origin navigations, with reduced-motion-safe fallbacks.

findings.summary: The long listing has no scroll-position feedback.
findings.evidence: The mobile page is 7,697px tall, but CSS inspection found no scroll-state query or progress indicator and the header does not adapt while scrolling.
findings.suggestedFix: Add a lightweight scroll progress or scroll-state-aware header treatment without obscuring content.

findings.summary: Advertising dominates and obscures the primary detail content.
findings.evidence: The detail screenshot shows a full-width 780x390 gambling ad before the player plus three fixed ads at z-index 9999, including a bottom overlay over content.
findings.suggestedFix: Remove load-time/fixed overlays from the primary flow; reserve bounded ad slots outside the player and make any transient ad clearly dismissible.

findings.summary: Ad overlays use custom fixed divs instead of semantic dismissible UI.
findings.evidence: The detail probe identifies #rdads-slider-l/r/f as fixed DIV elements at z-index 9999; no dialog or popover elements exist.
findings.suggestedFix: Use semantic popover/dialog primitives with accessible labels, focus handling, Escape and light-dismiss behavior where overlays are unavoidable.

findings.summary: Non-content chrome overwhelms the detail page.
findings.evidence: At 780x493 the detail screenshot is almost entirely header, navigation and gambling creative; the requested video content is not visible.
findings.suggestedFix: Reduce header/ad chrome and place the player and title in the initial content region.

findings.summary: Reusable cards and chips rely on viewport rules rather than container responsiveness.
findings.evidence: CSS inspection across reused card/chip templates found no @container or container-type rules.
findings.suggestedFix: Give reusable listing and metadata components containment and use size container queries where their layout changes.

findings.summary: Keyboard focus is not visible on most links.
findings.evidence: The focus probe found outline none 0px and no box shadow on navigation links and card links; only the search button had a visible 3px outline color.
findings.suggestedFix: Add a consistent high-contrast :focus-visible ring and retain it for all links, buttons, cards and player controls.

findings.summary: Opening a video does not lead directly to the player.
findings.evidence: The representative detail path lands on a large gambling ad and fixed overlays; the player is below the visible region.
findings.suggestedFix: Make the selected title/player the first primary content and keep advertising outside the task path.

findings.summary: Largest Contentful Paint is slow.
findings.evidence: Mobile Lighthouse reports LCP 4.5s and FCP 3.0s; the independent trace reports LCP 2.0s, showing material variability under test conditions.
findings.suggestedFix: Prioritise the actual LCP asset, remove render-blocking dependencies, and lazy-load below-fold media.

findings.summary: Images lack intrinsic dimensions.
findings.evidence: The image primitive reports all 62 images without width/height; Lighthouse reports CLS 0.084 and flags unsized images.
findings.suggestedFix: Emit width and height or aspect-ratio for every image and reserve stable card/media slots.

findings.summary: The critical path contains many blocking resources and weak caching.
findings.evidence: HAR/DOM confirmation shows nine parser-inserted stylesheets plus synchronous head scripts; Lighthouse estimates 2,110ms render-blocking savings and 1,039KiB cache savings.
findings.suggestedFix: Compile Tailwind at build time, remove unused player CSS from listings, defer noncritical scripts, self-host/subset fonts, and set durable immutable caching for versioned assets.

findings.summary: The homepage ships video-player code it does not use.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse finds about 385KiB unused JavaScript, including 88-91% waste in video.min.js and hls.js, plus 42KiB unused CSS; the homepage has no video element.
findings.suggestedFix: Conditionally load player/HLS/P2P dependencies only on detail pages and remove duplicate/unused WordPress and theme CSS.

findings.summary: Many card links have no accessible name.
findings.evidence: The semantic probe counts 65 blank-text links; Lighthouse link-name fails on full-card overlay anchors with no text or aria-label.
findings.suggestedFix: Give each card one descriptive linked heading or label overlay links with aria-labelledby.

findings.summary: Important text fails WCAG contrast.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse reports 2.22:1 for the primary heading prefix and 2.64-4.09:1 for highlighted labels against pale surfaces.
findings.suggestedFix: Use darker text/link tokens that meet 4.5:1 for normal text and test every state.

findings.summary: Focus visibility and heading structure are inconsistent.
findings.evidence: Most focused links compute to outline none; the homepage emits two H1 elements and 65 unnamed overlay links in the tab order.
findings.suggestedFix: Use one page H1, structured section headings, and visible :focus-visible styling; remove redundant tab stops.

findings.summary: Media lacks captions and at least one target is effectively unusable.
findings.evidence: The detail probe finds two video elements with zero track elements; Lighthouse target-size fails a 412x1 hit-counter link.
findings.suggestedFix: Provide caption/subtitle tracks or an equivalent transcript, remove the 1px interactive tracker link, and keep targets at least 24x24 CSS px.

findings.summary: Asset markup is unsound despite a valid document shell.
findings.evidence: The page has HTML5 doctype and UTF-8, but all 62 images omit dimensions and Lighthouse flags unsized assets.
findings.suggestedFix: Add intrinsic image dimensions and preserve aspect ratio in responsive CSS.

findings.summary: Many crawlable links have no descriptive link text.
findings.evidence: All links use real hrefs and robots allows indexing, but 65 anchors have no text or labelled image, confirmed by Lighthouse link-name failure.
findings.suggestedFix: Consolidate card links around descriptive titles or provide equivalent accessible names.

findings.summary: The public index has no working sitemap.
findings.evidence: robots.txt allows search crawling, canonical is present, but /sitemap.xml returns an nginx 404.
findings.suggestedFix: Publish a valid XML sitemap and reference it from robots.txt; keep canonical and indexing policies consistent.

findings.summary: The HTTPS page omits core security headers.
findings.evidence: The headers primitive reports no CSP, HSTS, X-Content-Type-Options, clickjacking policy, Referrer-Policy or Permissions-Policy.
findings.suggestedFix: Deploy a restrictive CSP, HSTS, nosniff, frame-ancestors, Referrer-Policy and a minimal Permissions-Policy.

findings.summary: The page sends substantial data to advertising/analytics third parties.
findings.evidence: Trackers finds five third-party origins; HAR records 12 third-party requests and 555,607 transferred bytes, including 425,720 bytes from rfr.darkadv.com and a Histats pixel.
findings.suggestedFix: Remove nonessential tracking and advertising dependencies, document the remaining purposes, and load them only with appropriate user choice.

findings.summary: Browser-enforced defensive policies are absent.
findings.evidence: The header audit found no HSTS, frame protection, Referrer-Policy, Permissions-Policy or CSP; no cookies or exposed secrets were observed.
findings.suggestedFix: Set HSTS, frame-ancestors, strict-origin-when-cross-origin or stricter referrer policy, and a least-privilege Permissions-Policy.

findings.summary: Fixed overlays cover the viewport rather than adapting safely.
findings.evidence: Three fixed custom ad elements use z-index 9999 and overlap the detail viewport; the bottom overlay spans 320px across the content area.
findings.suggestedFix: Keep transient UI inside safe viewport bounds, reserve space, and avoid fixed overlays over primary content.

findings.summary: The document language conflicts with the visible content.
findings.evidence: The semantic probe reports html lang="en-GB" while the navigation, headings and descriptions are predominantly Thai.
findings.suggestedFix: Set lang="th" on Thai pages and mark genuine English fragments with lang="en"; use logical CSS properties.

findings.summary: Date/status strings mix English into a Thai interface.
findings.evidence: Visible cards and detail metadata use strings such as “1 min ago”, “1 mins ago”, “14 hours ago” and “Added by” within otherwise Thai pages.
findings.suggestedFix: Format relative dates and metadata through an explicit Thai locale, with translation-ready message templates.

findings.summary: Advertising placement makes the destination and primary action hard to distinguish.
findings.evidence: The detail path opens on a large gambling creative with click-through plus fixed ad panels before the requested player; the small close control overlays the creative.
findings.suggestedFix: Clearly label advertising, keep it visually separate from player controls, avoid deceptive click surfaces, and make dismissal obvious and persistent.

findings.summary: Images are over-delivered and not responsive.
findings.evidence: The image primitive reports 61 images without srcset, 61 below-fold images without lazy loading, five oversized images and four legacy-format images; Lighthouse estimates 708KiB image savings.
findings.suggestedFix: Generate responsive AVIF/WebP srcsets, size to rendered slots, compress aggressively, and lazy-load below-fold thumbnails.

findings.summary: The listing eagerly fetches unused player code and below-fold media.
findings.evidence: HAR loads 92 requests/2.1MB; Lighthouse finds 385KiB unused JavaScript and the image audit finds 61 below-fold images without loading=lazy.
findings.suggestedFix: Conditionally load player bundles, lazy-load media, and defer background/noncritical requests until user intent.

findings.summary: Third-party and media cost is disproportionate on the listing.
findings.evidence: Images account for 1.35MB and third parties 556KB on a listing with no active video; ad-player scripts are among the largest transfers.
findings.suggestedFix: Set a route-specific byte budget, eliminate player/ad dependencies from listing pages, and cache/defer justified third parties.

taskList.title: Remove or relocate intrusive detail-page gambling overlays so the selected player is immediately reachable
Conditionally load player/ad dependencies and lazy-load responsive thumbnails
Restore accessible names, focus rings, contrast and caption equivalents
Deploy a complete browser security-header policy and reduce third-party collection
Add intrinsic image sizing and compile/defer critical resources
Set Thai language and locale-aware interface strings
Add preference-driven dark/high-contrast themes and modern responsive/transition enhancements
Publish a valid sitemap and descriptive linked-card markup
